review.translation: [And|0] [the springs of|1] [the deep|2] [and the floodgates of|3] [the heavens|4] [were shut|0], [and|5] [the rain|6] [from|7] [the heavens|8] [was held back|5].

analysis.evidence: The plural verb has two subjects, מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם (the springs of the deep) and אֲרֻבֹּת הַשָּׁמָיִם (the windows of the heavens). Both are openings through which the floodwaters came. The following clause says that the rain from the heavens was restrained, reinforcing the passive reading “were shut.”
analysis.morphology: Niphal wayyiqtol, third masculine plural, with prefixed וַ־.
analysis.sense: to be closed so that water can no longer flow through

analysis.evidence: מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם means “the springs of the deep.” The springs are shut along with the floodgates of heaven as the rain ceases.

In מַעְיְנֹת תְּהוֹם, “the springs of the deep,” תְּהוֹם names the waters that feed the springs. The verse pairs the closing of these springs below with the closing of the openings in the heavens above.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֲרֻבֹּת forms a construct phrase with הַשָּׁמָיִם, ‘the floodgates of the heavens’. These openings and the springs of the deep are the subjects of וַיִּסָּכְרוּ, ‘were closed’, and the next clause says the rain from the heavens stopped.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וַ־ ‘and’ prefixed to a feminine plural construct noun.

analysis.evidence: In וַאֲרֻבֹּת הַשָּׁמָיִם, “and the floodgates of the sky,” הַשָּׁמָיִם completes the construct phrase. The following clause says that rain from the sky ceased, identifying the sky as the source of the rain.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with the prefixed definite article הַ־.

analysis.evidence: The verb agrees with its masculine singular subject הַגֶּשֶׁם, “the rain.” In parallel with the closing of the springs and floodgates, מִן הַשָּׁמָיִם identifies the source from which the rain was withheld.
analysis.morphology: Niphal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: הַגֶּשֶׁם is the subject of וַיִּכָּלֵא ‘was held back’. The phrase מִן הַשָּׁמָיִם ‘from the heavens’ identifies the rain as the precipitation that stopped.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with the prefixed definite article הַ.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּכָּלֵא הַגֶּשֶׁם מִן הַשָּׁמָיִם, “the rain from the heavens was held back,” מִן marks the heavens as the source of the rain.
analysis.morphology: Independent preposition without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: out of, made from; from (a source or giver)

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּכָּלֵא הַגֶּשֶׁם מִן הַשָּׁמָיִם, the rain is held back. The separate preposition מִן marks the sky as the source from which the rain had been falling.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural noun in the absolute state with the prefixed definite article הַ־.
